A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COIN framework. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support comparison. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original COIN evaluations on six cell-segmentation datasets, component ablations and qualitative analyses, alongside reproduced and literature-reported baselines.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds an adaptive-threshold comparison and recursive self-distillation failure examples.

M1.justification: The three-stage pipeline, edge decoder and losses in Equations 1–11 are retained. However, v3 Appendix C.2 describes the confidence threshold as standard deviation divided by mean, whereas Section 3.2 in both versions defines it as their sum. The PDFs do not resolve whether this is an explanatory error or an intended scoring-rule change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate cell segmentation on MoNuSeg, TNBC, BRCA, CPM-17, CryoNuSeg and PanNuke. The new threshold analysis and failure examples reuse MoNuSeg. The removed open-vocabulary comparison also evaluated MoNuSeg segmentation, rather than separate dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 removes the supplementary comparison against Ferret, YOLO-World and GroundingDINO with SAM from v1 Appendix C.4 and Table 16. The main benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. UN-SAM is added only to the conceptual comparison in Table 1, without reported evaluation results.

E3.justification: v3 Appendix C.2 introduces a controlled comparison of adaptive thresholding against fixed thresholds ranging from 0.1 to 0.8, tracking MoNuSeg test IoU through 100 epochs. Retained benchmark metrics and stated evaluation procedures are unchanged. The newly disclosed 100-epoch budget does not establish a change to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds an adaptive-versus-fixed threshold ablation, training-trajectory and confidence-dispersion analysis in Figure 12, and persistent failure examples in Appendix D.3 and Figure 17. Existing component, backbone, adjacent-cell and edge-decoder analyses remain. OT sensitivity analysis is relocated from Appendix B.7 to C.1.

E5.justification: Figure 12 newly reports standard deviation across instance-level confidence scores and a min–max IoU range across fixed thresholds. This adds limited dispersion and model-uncertainty reporting, not repeated-run uncertainty estimates. Neither version supplies experimental seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 and matched retained ablation tables preserve their numerical results; for example, SSA+COIN remains at 0.580 AJI and 0.536 PQ on MoNuSeg. v3 newly reports roughly a three-percentage-point IoU advantage for adaptive thresholding, saturation near epoch 40 and failure examples. The open-vocabulary results in v1 Table 16 are removed.

T1.justification: The existing equations remain, and the new OT push-operation subsection restates Equation 4 rather than supplying new theory. However, Appendix C.2 introduces a mathematically incompatible ratio description of the threshold alongside the retained mean-plus-standard-deviation definition. This is a limited inconsistency in the mathematical description; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same central claims: annotation-free, model-agnostic confidence-guided distillation, recovery of accurate instances, and superior reported segmentation performance. The added introductory hypotheses explain these retained contributions rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations of selection as implicit memory and adaptive thresholds as filtering early noisy labels. It explicitly acknowledges persistent errors when propagation misses transparent cells. Conversely, removing v1 Appendix C.4 also removes its interpretation of open-vocabulary failures as a domain gap and its parameter-efficiency argument.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies 100 training epochs and describes USS processing once per image and SAM use each epoch. The abstract replaces the direct repository pointer with a project-page pointer. Removing v1 Appendix C.4 and Table 16 also removes comparator prompting and inference-model-size information. These documentation changes do not establish changed execution of retained experiments.

R1.justification: v3 adds a UN-SAM reference and expands conceptual Table 1 to include UN-SAM and the already-cited InstaSAM. It removes references to Ferret, YOLO-World and GroundingDINO with their supplementary comparison. The principal related-work discussion and novelty positioning otherwise remain.

P1.justification: The introduction gains two explicit hypotheses, SAM-consistency explanations expand, and several appendix subsections are added or relocated. Author affiliations and acknowledgments are updated. Most existing prose and the overall introduction–method–experiments narrative remain closely matched.

P2.justification: The main text and textual appendices are extensively reformatted from one column to two, with figures and tables resized and repositioned. Table 3 consolidates four dataset groups into one wide display, and Table 1 gains columns. v3 also adds Figures 12 and 17 and removes v1 Table 16. This substantially changes visual organization.

improvement.justification: The threshold ablation and explicit failure examples improve support for design choices and transparency about limitations while retaining the core benchmark evidence. However, the new threshold explanation contradicts the existing definition, leaving the basis of the added analysis unclear, and the supplementary comparator removal narrows comparison breadth. These benefits and the unresolved reproducibility problem prevent a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
